questions.prompt: Calculate \(\mathbf e_1\cdot(3,-2,5)\), where \(\mathbf e_1=(1,0,0)\).
questions.answer:
We need the component along the first Cartesian unit vector.
Method: Use the Euclidean dot product.
\[\mathbf e_1\cdot(3,-2,5)=1(3)+0(-2)+0(5)=3.\]
Final answer: \(3\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the norm of \(\mathbf v=(3,4,0)\).
questions.answer:
We need the Euclidean norm of the vector.
Method: Take the square root of the self-dot product.
\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2+0^2}=\sqrt{25}=5.\]
Final answer: \(|\mathbf v|=5\).

questions.prompt: Construct a unit vector parallel to \(\mathbf v=(2,-2,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need to normalize the given vector.
Method: Divide the vector by its norm.
\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3,\qquad \hat{\mathbf v}=\frac{\mathbf v}{|\mathbf v|}=\left(\frac23,-\frac23,\frac13\right).\]
Final answer: \(\hat{\mathbf v}=(2/3,-2/3,1/3)\).

questions.prompt: Test whether \(\mathbf a=(1,2,-1)\) and \(\mathbf b=(3,-1,1)\) are orthogonal.
questions.answer:
We need to test the orthogonality condition.
Method: Compute the dot product and compare it with zero.
\[\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=1(3)+2(-1)+(-1)(1)=3-2-1=0.\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf a\perp\mathbf b\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the projection of \(\mathbf b=(4,2)\) onto \(\mathbf a=(1,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need the component of (mathbf b) parallel to (mathbf a).
Method: Use (operatorname{proj}_{mathbf a}mathbf b=(mathbf acdotmathbf b/|mathbf a|^2)mathbf a).
\[\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=6,\quad |\mathbf a|^2=2,\quad \operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b=\frac62(1,1)=(3,3).\]
Final answer: \(\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b=(3,3)\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the component of \(\mathbf b=(4,2)\) perpendicular to \(\mathbf a=(1,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need the remainder after removing the parallel projection.
Method: Subtract the projection from the original vector.
\[\mathbf b_{\parallel}=(3,3),\qquad \mathbf b_{\perp}=\mathbf b-\mathbf b_{\parallel}=(4,2)-(3,3)=(1,-1).\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf b_{\perp}=(1,-1)\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the components of \(\mathbf b=(2,3,4)\) parallel and perpendicular to \(\mathbf a=(0,1,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need both orthogonal components of the decomposition.
Method: Project onto the non-unit direction and subtract.
\[c=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}=\frac{7}{2},\quad \mathbf b_{\parallel}=\left(0,\frac72,\frac72\right),\quad \mathbf b_{\perp}=\left(2,-\frac12,\frac12\right).\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf b_{\parallel}=(0,7/2,7/2)\), \(\mathbf b_{\perp}=(2,-1/2,1/2)\).

questions.prompt: Verify the orthogonality of the two components obtained by projecting \(\mathbf b=(1,4,2)\) onto \(\mathbf a=(2,0,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need the decomposition and its dot-product check.
Method: Project, subtract, then calculate the component dot product.
\[c=\frac{4}{5},\quad \mathbf b_{\parallel}=\left(\frac85,0,\frac45\right),\quad \mathbf b_{\perp}=\left(-\frac35,4,\frac65\right).\]\[\mathbf b_{\parallel}\cdot\mathbf b_{\perp}=-\frac{24}{25}+\frac{24}{25}=0.\]
Final answer: The components are \((8/5,0,4/5)\) and \((-3/5,4,6/5)\), with dot product \(0\).

questions.prompt: Construct the matrix for orthogonal projection onto the line spanned by \(\mathbf a=(1,2)\).
questions.answer:
We need the linear map that projects every vector onto the given line.
Method: Use (P=mathbf amathbf a^{mathsf T}/(mathbf a^{mathsf T}mathbf a)).
\[\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a=5,\]\[P=\frac15\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}.\]
Final answer: \(P=\frac15\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the projection of \(\mathbf b=(2,-1,3)\) onto the plane with unit normal \(\mathbf n=(0,0,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need the component of the vector lying in the plane.
Method: Subtract the normal component ((mathbf ncdotmathbf b)mathbf n).
\[\mathbf b_{\rm plane}=\mathbf b-(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf b)\mathbf n=(2,-1,3)-3(0,0,1)=(2,-1,0).\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf b_{\rm plane}=(2,-1,0)\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the projection of \(\mathbf v=(2,1,3)\) onto the subspace spanned by the orthonormal vectors \(\mathbf e_1=(1,0,0)\) and \(\mathbf e_2=(0,1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2)\).
questions.answer:
We need the sum of the two orthonormal projections.
Method: Use (sum_i(mathbf e_icdotmathbf v)mathbf e_i).
\[\mathbf e_1\cdot\mathbf v=2,\qquad \mathbf e_2\cdot\mathbf v=\frac4{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2,\]\[\operatorname{proj}\mathbf v=2\mathbf e_1+2\sqrt2\mathbf e_2=(2,2,2).\]
Final answer: The subspace projection is \((2,2,2)\).

questions.prompt: Verify that \(P=\frac15\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\) satisfies \(P^2=P\).
questions.answer:
We need to check idempotence of the projection matrix.
Method: Multiply the matrix by itself.
\[P^2=\frac1{25}\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}=\frac1{25}\begin{pmatrix}5&10\\10&20\end{pmatrix}=\frac15\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}=P.\]
Final answer: \(P^2=P\).

questions.prompt: Determine all real \(k\) for which \((1,k,2)\) is orthogonal to \((2,-1,3)\).
questions.answer:
We need the parameter values that make the dot product zero.
Method: Form and solve the orthogonality equation.
\[(1,k,2)\cdot(2,-1,3)=2-k+6=8-k.\]\[8-k=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad k=8.\]
Final answer: \(k=8\).

questions.prompt: Find the distance from \(\mathbf p=(3,1)\) to the line spanned by \(\mathbf a=(1,2)\).
questions.answer:
We need the norm of the component perpendicular to the line.
Method: Project (mathbf p) onto (mathbf a), subtract, and take the norm.
\[\mathbf p_{\parallel}=\frac{5}{5}(1,2)=(1,2),\qquad \mathbf p_{\perp}=(2,-1),\]\[d=|\mathbf p_{\perp}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt5.\]
Final answer: The distance is \(\sqrt5\).

questions.prompt: Derive the parallel and perpendicular components of \(\mathbf b\) relative to a nonzero vector \(\mathbf a\).
questions.answer:
We need formulas valid for arbitrary vectors.
Method: Write the parallel component as (cmathbf a) and impose perpendicularity on the remainder.
\[\mathbf b_{\perp}=\mathbf b-c\mathbf a,\qquad 0=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b_{\perp}=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b-c|\mathbf a|^2.\]\[c=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}.\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf b_{\parallel}=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b_{\perp}=\mathbf b-\mathbf b_{\parallel}\).

questions.prompt: Determine all real \(k\) for which the projection of \((k,2)\) onto \((1,1)\) equals \((3,3)\).
questions.answer:
We need the parameter that gives the specified projection.
Method: Equate the projection coefficient to three.
\[\operatorname{proj}_{(1,1)}(k,2)=\frac{k+2}{2}(1,1).\]\[\frac{k+2}{2}=3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad k=4.\]
Final answer: \(k=4\).

questions.prompt: Construct an orthonormal basis of the plane spanned by \(\mathbf v_1=(1,1,0)\) and \(\mathbf v_2=(1,0,1)\).
questions.answer:
We need to apply Gram-Schmidt to the two spanning vectors.
Method: Normalize the first vector, remove its projection from the second, then normalize.
\[\mathbf e_1=\frac1{\sqrt2}(1,1,0).\]\[\mathbf u_2=\mathbf v_2-(\mathbf e_1\cdot\mathbf v_2)\mathbf e_1=(1,0,1)-\frac12(1,1,0)=\left(\frac12,-\frac12,1\right).\]\[|\mathbf u_2|=\sqrt{\frac32},\qquad \mathbf e_2=\frac1{\sqrt6}(1,-1,2).\]
Final answer: An orthonormal basis is \(\{(1,1,0)/\sqrt2,(1,-1,2)/\sqrt6\}\).

questions.prompt: Prove that \(\mathbf b-\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b\) is orthogonal to every nonzero \(\mathbf a\).
questions.answer:
We need to prove the defining perpendicularity property.
Method: Substitute the projection formula and take the dot product with (mathbf a).
\[\mathbf a\cdot\left(\mathbf b-\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}\mathbf a\right)=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b-\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}|\mathbf a|^2=0.\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf b-\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b\perp\mathbf a\).

questions.prompt: Prove that projection onto a line is unchanged when its spanning vector \(\mathbf a\) is replaced by \(c\mathbf a\), where \(c\ne0\).
questions.answer:
We need to compare the two projection formulas.
Method: Substitute the scaled spanning vector and cancel the scalar factors.
\[\operatorname{proj}_{c\mathbf a}\mathbf b=\frac{(c\mathbf a)\cdot\mathbf b}{|c\mathbf a|^2}(c\mathbf a)=\frac{c(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b)}{c^2|\mathbf a|^2}c\mathbf a=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}\mathbf a.\]
Final answer: \(\operatorname{proj}_{c\mathbf a}\mathbf b=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b\).

questions.prompt: Prove that \(P=\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}/(\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a)\) is symmetric and idempotent for every nonzero real column vector \(\mathbf a\).
questions.answer:
We need to verify the two projection-matrix identities.
Method: Use transpose rules and associate the scalar middle product.
\[P^{\mathsf T}=\frac{(\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}}{\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a}=\frac{\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}}{\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a}=P.\]\[P^2=\frac{\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}}{(\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a)^2}=\frac{\mathbf a(\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a)\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}}{(\mathbf a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf a)^2}=P.\]
Final answer: \(P^{\mathsf T}=P\) and \(P^2=P\).
